author: Jakson Gudawela
headline: Oman's manufacturing show opens with one named sponsor and an open call for abstracts
deck: IMPEX26 arrives in Muscat with a defined sector scope and very little else published.
excerpt: IMPEX26 opens at the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre on 21 September with seven declared exhibit profiles, one named sponsor and no published exhibitor list.
content:
IMPEX26, an industrial manufacturing and process engineering exhibition, runs at the Grand Ballroom of the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre in Muscat from 21 to 23 September, organised by Innoway Technologies. It covers seven declared exhibit profiles across manufacturing and process engineering, with abstract submission open.

Beyond that, very little has been published. One sponsor is named — Machineryline India. No exhibitor list, conference programme, speaker roster, visitor target or exhibitor target has been released, and no supporting government body is identified. For an event opening in under two weeks in a market where government backing is usually prominent, that is a thin disclosure record.

The subject matter is genuine enough. Oman's industrial base outside oil and gas has been expanding, and this publication has reported the pieces: OMR200m of industrial projects signed across Duqm, Salalah and Khazaen; Oman Arab Bank's $200m participation in the Sohar polysilicon plant, part of a $1.6bn raise that has since brought first production; and the free zone development at Sohar and Duqm that anchors most of it.

That base creates a real market for process engineering services and equipment. A polysilicon plant, an aluminium smelter, a refinery and a fertiliser complex all require maintenance engineering, instrumentation, materials handling and the industrial services that keep them running, and Oman's domestic supplier base for those is thinner than Saudi Arabia's or the UAE's. An exhibition addressing it is a reasonable proposition.

The timing places it a week after Oman Climate Week at the same venue, which for a visitor travelling to Muscat is either convenient or an awkward split depending on how the two audiences overlap. Climate Week has published a 27-name steering committee, a full session programme and a tiered sponsor list including Petroleum Development Oman, OQ and Oman LNG. The contrast between the two events at the same venue in the same month is stark.

An abstract call still open this close to the event suggests a technical programme still being assembled rather than one finalised, which limits what can be said about the content in advance.

Anyone considering attendance should approach the organiser directly for an exhibitor list before committing travel. The detail here is drawn from the organiser's own site, which is the only source carrying it. Oman's industrial expansion is real; whether this particular exhibition is the venue where it gets served is harder to judge from what has been released. A direct approach to the organiser is the only reliable way to establish who will actually be on the floor.
